scope: Candidate F complete bounded code-area review at exact supplied source hashes; standard-library worker-host API, Go 1.22 minimum.

coverage.reason: Applicable: the host-supplied Lease protocol, injected Open dependency, cancellation/error propagation and cohort ownership are design boundaries; reviewed API, ownership and composition without demanding another framework.
Applicable: reviewed local state transitions, result collection, checked errors, context guards, docs, value/closure semantics under go 1.22; gofmt and vet independently executed.

Applicable: reviewed every README result/lifecycle obligation, API shape, empty/finite/open input, partial acquisition, all three failure stages, cancellation before/during/stopping, successful effects and supported Go minimum.

Applicable: reviewed candidate host_test.go assertions, doubles, event gates, cleanup and whether meaningful contract violations evade its authored suite. External held/supplementary/independent probes verify behavior; they are not additions to the candidate regression suite.

Not applicable within this bounded trusted-host API: Job is a caller-supplied integer; Open and Lease are trusted collaborators; there is no demonstrated attacker, authorization boundary, sensitive sink, credential, cryptographic or network/file parsing decision. General resource failures are not recast as vulnerabilities. No advisory scan or security assessment of an unspecified host is claimed.

Applicable: cancellation, stop propagation, failure containment, joining actual cleanup and errors.Is diagnostics are the available library signals. No service telemetry, retries or arbitrary timeout requirement is inferred.

Applicable: limit bounds acquired leases through Close, cohort completion controls goroutines/resources, and available capacity must be used. Assessed scaling/lifetime and bounded event counts; no microbenchmark or production latency claim.

Applicable: go.mod declares Go 1.22 and standard-library-only production/tests. Verified standalone readonly resolution, host and actual minimum compilation/test execution, imports, module graph and exact input hashes. No generated/native/release inputs or bit-identical artifact contract.

Not applicable to the bounded library code area: no configured release artifact, CI/promotion path, process signals, container, runtime configuration, health/routing or grace budget decision is supplied or promised. Host deployment evidence is unavailable outside scope and excluded, not reported as passing. Library lifecycle is assessed by the applicable topics.

findings.cause: The cohort context is unconditionally canceled when admission ends, even for a healthy full cohort or normal input closure.
findings.evidence: candidates/F/host.go:93; candidates/F/host.go:94; evidence/F-host-independent.log: healthy two-job cohort sees canceled context before release and returns both Run cancellation errors; evidence/F-minimum-independent.log: same intended assertions; Healthy cooperative Runs are stopped before their requested work completes, and completed uncanceled input returns a failure. This is a contained important success/lifecycle contract failure.
findings.correction: Cancel only for an observed failure/caller stop; join normal Runs without canceling their work, then release leases.

findings.cause: A successful Open always calls Run without checking that stopping happened during acquisition.
findings.evidence: candidates/F/host.go:84; candidates/F/host.go:85; evidence/F-host-independent.log: callback cancellation-before-success still starts one Run; evidence/F-minimum-independent.log: same intended assertion; evidence/F-host-contract.log: held acquired-before-stop fixture detects forbidden Run; The explicit fixture requires a lease acquired before stop to remain owned but unstarted; F starts it after caller cancellation and later closes it. One contained important startup/stop failure.
findings.correction: Record acquired lease ownership, observe stop before Run entry, and skip Run while joining/releasing all prior work.

findings.cause: Capacity is decremented on Run completion while the acquired lease remains unreleased until later cohort Close.
findings.evidence: candidates/F/host.go:38; candidates/F/host.go:61; candidates/F/host.go:103; evidence/F-host-independent.log: TestIndependentCompletedRunsRetainCapacity records peak=8 with limit 2; evidence/F-minimum-independent.log: same measured peak=8; evidence/F-host-race.log: three repeated peak=8 intended assertions; Eight paced successful jobs on open input retain eight acquired leases at capacity 2, with no Close until input ends. Peak is 4x declared bound for eight jobs; for a stream of completed Runs retention grows with jobs rather than limit. This is a contained major resource and lifecycle-contract failure; no unobserved system exhaustion is claimed.
findings.correction: Track acquired leases and pending reservations through completed Close, and stop admitting once those owned slots reach limit; completion alone cannot release capacity.

findings.cause: Healthy capacity fixtures ignore their Run contexts, so premature coordinated stop is invisible.
findings.evidence: candidates/F/host_test.go:33; candidates/F/host_test.go:78; candidates/F/host_test.go:148; evidence/F-host-authored.log: suite passes P1; evidence/F-host-independent.log: cooperative healthy Run contexts detect premature cancellation; The important uncanceled success contract is tested with callbacks that keep succeeding after any stop request. Their gates verify sequencing while masking whether work was allowed to complete cooperatively.
findings.correction: Make healthy callbacks verify they are not canceled before their external success gate and return ctx.Err when improperly stopped.

findings.cause: Authored cancellation coverage does not exercise an acquired success returned after stopping and assert no Run.
findings.evidence: candidates/F/host_test.go:135; candidates/F/host_test.go:259; evidence/F-host-authored.log: suite passes P2; evidence/F-host-independent.log: forbidden Run after callback cancellation; Input-wait/already-canceled tests do not protect the important partial acquisition ownership transition.
findings.correction: Return a successful lease after callback cancellation, assert zero Runs, and still require owned Close after cohort join.

findings.cause: Capacity tests inspect only a full initial cohort and later Run starts, without counting live acquired leases across completed Runs on open input.
findings.evidence: candidates/F/host_test.go:33; candidates/F/host_test.go:78; candidates/F/host_test.go:148; evidence/F-host-authored.log: suite passes P3; evidence/F-host-independent.log: eight held leases at capacity 2; An explicit important capacity bound through Close is effectively unverified for a stream of successful completions; Run concurrency is insufficient as its proxy.
findings.correction: Track live acquisition/release counts and use paced successful jobs on open input to assert the lease bound, plus held Close.

strengths.evidence: The exact Job/Lease/Serve API remains compatible and construction stays host-owned through the Open function, with no unrelated framework/public API; both actual toolchains compile every source package.

Actual go1.22.12 and go1.26.5 compile the standalone go 1.22 standard-library-only module with GOWORK=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly; go list -m all returns only example.com/service-owned-workers. No external go.sum is needed.
